description: Cross-org alert-metric read surface (§8 Q0b slice 2, issue #172). ONE golden, TWO stacks: TS `applyAlertMetricFloor` / `isSensitiveAlertMetric` / `ALERT_METRICS_VIA_CSHARP` (packages/api/src/repositories/alert-evaluation.repository.ts, asserted by tests/monitoring/alert-metrics-fixtures.test.ts) and C# `Tims.Domain.AlertMetrics.AlertMetricKeys` + `KAnonymity.SuppressBelowMin5` (asserted by Tims.UnitTests/AlertMetrics/AlertMetricsFixtureTests.cs). The thing this pins is the §21 min-5 floor AND which metrics it applies to: an alert RULE is an exact-count oracle (a rule `metric eq 3` that fires recovers a sub-floor count over a restricted population without ever calling a read endpoint), so a sensitive 1..4 must become null/suppressed on BOTH sides. The two directions are asymmetric and both are wrong in a different way: flooring too little re-opens the oracle on salary_adjustments, flooring too much silently disables active_surveys alerting for every small org.

sensitivity.name: active_surveys counts survey DEFINITIONS, not responses — NOT a §21-restricted model
pending_salary_adjustments counts SalaryAdjustment rows — restricted, so floored

floor.name: sensitive, 0 — an EMPTY bucket reveals no individual, so it passes through unfloored
sensitive, 1 — sub-floor, suppressed (a rule `eq 1` must not be able to fire)
sensitive, 4 — the LAST suppressed value; off-by-one here re-opens the oracle
sensitive, 5 — the FIRST value that passes; off-by-one here silently disables the alert
sensitive, 7 — well above the floor, unchanged
NON-sensitive, 1 — NOT floored. An org with one active survey must still alert; flooring everything is the plausible-looking bug this row exists to catch
NON-sensitive, 4 — NOT floored, for the same reason

metricKeys.name: headcount is a real ALERT_METRIC_KEY but is NOT served here — `users` does not flip, so it stays on the TS Prisma path
active_alerts is real but not served — `alerts` does not flip
vacancies_open_60d is real but not served — `vacancies` does not flip
sla_active_breaches is real but not served — it is computed in app code over applications
an unknown key is refused, never defaulted to a metric
case is exact — ACTIVE_SURVEYS is refused
